# Agent design

The target architecture of our buyer, merged from the team's planning notes (PRs #7 to #10,
10 Oct). What we learned in play is in `learnings.md`; this file says what we build.

**Status.** The branch `steffen/price-engine` plays a code-only policy with a model-written
paragraph (`buyer/policy.py`, run by `buyer/runner.py`): practice mean of best scores 0.73 (from
0.32), sandbox D01 0.99, D02 0.73. What it does is under "Implemented" below; the rest of this file
is the target design. Julian's draft two (`origin/julian/draft-two`) holds a richer stance and
reader design that is not merged. The architecture diagram is on page 1 of
[how-it-works.pdf](how-it-works.pdf).

## Implemented (price engine)

| Module | Job |
|---|---|
| `buyer/economics.py` | C of a sheet; the accept gate (`deal_cost`); what a sheet is worth to the supplier (`supplier_value` plus overtime for a faster delivery than it quoted); term planning: every allowed combination priced at the supplier's own valuation, lowest C, ties to the supplier's side; the relationship-optimal price |
| `buyer/claims.py` | claim bank: should-cost below its price, our order prices, falling cost-driver indices, notice period, forecast, scorecard, case rival quotes, hedge and open-book notes; rival offers in an RFQ |
| `buyer/personas.py` | owner type, persona signals from notes, letters, quote remarks and news, cost of money |
| `buyer/policy.py` | per thread: anchor by goal and persona, 30 % of the gap per round, held low after a deep first concession, patience budget for near-cost, fully booked and relationship-goal suppliers; adopts its counter terms when they cost us less, mirrors a better alternative, takes a required index clause; claims 3 in round 1, then 1 per round; close on final offer, agreement or round limit |
| `buyer/reader.py` | the supplier's asks from its fixed sentences (volume, proof, faster payment, our target); no model |
| `buyer/writer.py`, `buyer/llm.py` | the e-mail: a model paragraph that answers the supplier's last e-mail and its asks (no digits, IDs or leaks, else the template), then code sentences with figures (the binding volume), claims and the proposal from code; the forecast rows as a CSV when proof is asked |
| `buyer/runner.py` | one message at a time per session, to the thread whose 60 s clock has run longest; keepalive questions for finished bidders; rollback when a send times out; a guarded move resends our last sheet; the model's time budgeted so every live clock still gets a message; a terminal reply ends the case; accept the cheapest standing sheet that keeps the must-haves and beats the alternative (relationship charge included), after a refused close decide again on what stands; Live Final waves that never raise and resume a crashed case |

## Principle

Code owns every number and every binding decision; the model reads replies and writes e-mails.
Score is total cost C, not price. Every step has a fallback that still sends a move within 60 s.

## A case

1. **Prepare** (before the first move, about 20 s): open the session, build a case brief: C_open,
   C_alt, target, walk-away, the lever table (C of each allowed option), a view of each supplier,
   and a claim bank of verified arguments. A stance call proposes per-supplier parameters; code
   clamps them.
2. **Negotiate**, one thread negotiator per supplier, in parallel. Each round:

   ```
   supplier reply
     -> READ    (model, hard timeout)  offer, intent, objections, statements
     -> CHECK   (code)  supplier statements against the data
     -> PLAN    (code)  candidate sheets scored with total_cost, filtered by must_haves_ok
     -> DECIDE  (code)  counter / accept / walk away, move size, claims
     -> WRITE   (model, hard timeout; template if late)  figures and IDs injected by code
     -> GUARD   (code)  every negotiable field, claim format, no leaks, no unplanned figures
   ```

3. **Close**: accept the best sheet that keeps every must-have and beats C_alt, or walk away;
   at the latest 90 s before the wave's 8-minute cap.
4. **Learn**: store the trace and what we learned per supplier for the next practice run.

## Modules

| Module | Job | Run by |
|---|---|---|
| Runner | polls the final's case list, one coordinator per case, restarts after a crash | code |
| Coordinator | case brief, starts thread negotiators, shared state, decides when to close | code |
| Economics | C of any sheet, floor, anchor, target, concession steps, accept gate | code |
| Personas | one profile per supplier: traits with evidence, levers, history | model offline, code live |
| Claim bank | arguments as sentences with figure and data ID, computed as the arena checks them | code |
| Reader / writer | supplier e-mail to JSON; move to e-mail | small model, hard timeout |
| Fact check | supplier statements: confirmed, contradicted, selective, unverifiable (not built) | code |
| Guard | blocks leaks, unknown IDs, unplanned figures, broken must-haves | code |
| Fallback cascade | unknown supplier or part: case facts, data search, category averages, its documents | code |

## What feeds the brief, by impact

| # | Data | Decides | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | case file, quote PDF | C directly: need, horizon, rates, must-haves, alternative, options, standard terms | `GET /v1/cases`, `arena_kit.docs.standard_terms` |
| 2 | supplier cost floor | anchor, target, relationship charge | `should_cost`, cost-breakdown XLSX on request |
| 3 | index values of its cost drivers | justified price change, strongest claims | `cost_drivers`, `index_values`, `facts.json` |
| 4 | letters, notes, news | what moves it (cash, capacity, relationship), notice periods | `documents`, `correspondence/`, `news` |
| 5 | negotiation history | how far it usually moves | `negotiation_history` |
| 6 | intel, our invoices | archetype, payment lever | `supplier_intel`, `invoices`, `suppliers` (cash discount) |
| 7 | contracts and clauses | notice, index clauses, expiry, single sourcing | `contracts`, `contract_clauses`, `sourcing` |
| 8 | scorecards, QNs | quality lever | `scorecards`, `quality_notifications` |
| 9 | forecasts, PO prices, rival quotes | volume, price history, rival arguments | `forecast_lines`, `po_lines`, `quotes` |

The Sunday release (`data/release-sunday/`) and the case's own `facts` are read at runtime.

## Supplier estimate

`arena_kit.cost.supplier_value` prices a deal for the supplier from `standard`, `interest_rate`,
`ppm` and `extra`; `relationship_cost` needs `full_cost` and is 0 without it. So we estimate:

- **Full cost**: cost-breakdown XLSX, else `should_cost` moved by its drivers' index change, else
  quote minus an assumed margin. A relationship charge in a practice result reveals the true margin.
- **Cost of money**: cash discounts, cash-need notes, credit index, equity ratio. Seen rates: 0 to
  17 %/yr (`learnings.md`).
- **Extra**: overtime for speed (negative) or idle capacity filled by volume (positive), only from
  evidence. Volume, contract length and index clauses are not cash in `supplier_value`.

C_best estimate: the cheapest allowed sheet whose supplier value stays above its floor, or C_alt.

## Policy

A stance per supplier (opening gap, capture, margin, justified share, steps) proposed by the model
at case open, clamped by code to a range per tier and goal, logged with a reason. Fallback
constants when the stance call times out:

| Constant | Values |
|---|---|
| capture (share of possible saving before accepting) | leverage 0.75, quality_first 0.65, stabilise 0.6, secure_supply 0.55, routine 0.5 |
| opening gap below the quote (never below the floor) | strategic 5 %, important 8 %, standard 12 % |
| margin above full cost for the floor | case's `sustainable_margin_pct` in `stabilise` / `secure_supply`, else strategic 4 %, important 2 %, standard 0 % |
| justified share offered in round 1 of a price increase | strategic 0.5, important 0.25, standard 0 |
| concession steps, only after the supplier moved | 35, 25, 15, 10 % of the remaining gap |

Live signals adjust within bounds: approval needed shrinks steps (x0.7), high walk risk stops
price pushes. At the target, hold one more round while the supplier still moves.

## Build order

1. Accept and walk-away guard with `total_cost` and `must_haves_ok`.
2. Term search: every combination of allowed options, scored with standard terms for unstated
   fields. Fixes coverage and index-clause losses.
3. Supplier estimate: full cost and cost of money, giving target and walk-away.
4. Claim bank from `facts.json` and the index tables.
5. Persona reading and pacing.
6. Tune on practice traces, one change per batch.

## Generalise

- Branch on features (goal, must-haves, credit, cash signals, owner type, quote content), never on
  case or supplier IDs. No constants copied from one case.
- Hold out two or three practice cases for checking only.
- Test failure paths: late model call, malformed reply, a supplier that refuses everything,
  missing quote fields, a quote PDF without a standard-terms section.
- Change the agent only for a lesson seen in two cases or clearly general. Freeze early.

## Tactics

Use: data-backed anchors, requests framed as trades, two or three packages to watch the choice,
shrinking concessions with an ask in return, real rival offers cited by ID, a recap of every field
before closing.

Avoid: invented figures or rival offers (`contradicted`), bluffed urgency or walk-aways (no
effect, `learnings.md`), squeezing a weak supplier in `stabilise` / `secure_supply`, leaking
urgency, budget, target or a missing alternative. Prompt injection of supplier bots counts as an
attack on the arena: never.
# Generalisation to the Live Final

How well the agent on `steffen/price-engine` (commit `9182604`) should carry over to Sunday: new
suppliers, up to a third of cases mixing supplier and case types practice never showed, some
citing the 08:00 release. Research on Saturday 10 October, evening: the kit's code, all 21 case
files, `logs/runs/`, `exports/`, the data package, and our agent on `arena-sim`. No practice
quota spent. Same conventions as `learnings.md`: date, tag, finding, evidence, consequence.

## Verdict

The code runs on every case structure we know. Its tuning is in-sample and unmeasured beyond
the ten hosted cases. The biggest gaps for Sunday: new suppliers get a neutral profile because
the release's letters and news never reach the persona code; one exception loses a whole case
(or every later wave); four or more bidders time out.

| # | Risk | Damage | Fix | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | an exception in a move or the wave poll | a case at its alternative (0 in 6 of 21), or all later waves | catch per move, keep polling | small |
| 2 | release rows invisible to SQL; most suppliers without text | neutral profile for new suppliers | read release rows via the ID index; scan the supplier's e-mails | small to medium |
| 3 | 4 or more bidders | timeouts, lost patience, ended threads | stop sending to the worst bidders after round 1 | medium, a tactics decision |
| 4 | missed phrasings in `SIGNALS` | traits not detected | widen to word stems | small |
| 5 | `price_unit` ignored | wrong-direction rival or order-price claims | divide by `price_unit` | small |

## Findings

### Robustness

- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Every known case structure runs end to end.** All 21 public case files,
  including the nine never hosted (P06, P09, P12 to P17, P19), played through `arena-sim`
  in-process with our agent and the package, no model: no exception, 0 to 1 s per case. Covers
  bundles (P07 4 parts, P15 3), the 3-bidder RFQ, `tooling_eur` (P06) and up to 75 term
  combinations (P09). The sim's supplier is a fixed script, so this checks code paths, not
  tactics. → Worth a test in `tests/` that plays every case file from `GET /v1/cases` this way
  (load them into `Sim(cases, pkg.facts)`, strip the `hosted` key).
- 2026-10-10 `rules` **One exception loses a case.** `play_case` has no guard around
  `Negotiator.setup` or `move`. Fields a hidden case may lack crash it: a rival quote without
  `unit_price` (`claims.py` `rival_quote`), an index clause without `material_share`
  (`writer.py` `FIELDS`), a scorecard without `quarter` (`claims.py` `scorecard`), a month not in
  `YYYY-MM` (`months_back`). The session then sits until the wave cap, which scores the
  alternative (0 in D01, P05, P06, P10, P14, P17). → Catch per move; on error send our last
  sheet again with the template e-mail.
- 2026-10-10 `rules` **One error stops the final.** `runner.play_waves` re-raises any non-403
  `ArenaError` from the case-list poll, and a network error after the client's retries is not
  caught at all (`arena_kit/client.py` `_call`). Every later wave is then lost; no human may
  restart. → Catch everything in the poll loop, log, sleep, poll again; a crashed case resumes
  with `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` (a second `POST` is a 409 naming the session).

### Timing

- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Four bidders or more time out.** The arena answers one call per session at
  a time (`arena_kit/client.py`: "a call may wait for another call on the same session first").
  Supplier replies took 19 s median, 28 s p90 (121 moves in `logs/runs/`); our writer 1.8 s
  median, 6.3 s max (73 calls, none failed, 7 dropped by the filter). A thread waits about
  (N - 1) x 21 s for its next message against a 60 s limit:

  | Bidders | Wait at median | Wait at p90 | Rounds per thread in 390 s |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 2 | 23 s | 34 s | 9 / 6 |
  | 3 | 44 s | 66 s, late | 6 / 4 |
  | 4 | 65 s, late | late | 5 / 3 |

  P05 (3 bidders) had one late move in v5. No case file has more than 3 bidders, but hidden
  cases bring "new settings". → With 4 or more bidders, stop sending to the clearly worst ones
  after round 1; the writer's 20 s timeout matters little next to the supplier's reply time.

### Data and the Sunday release

- 2026-10-10 `rules` **The release reaches only part of the agent.** `DataPackage` finds
  `data/release-sunday/` next to the package, merges its `facts.json` (new IDs only) and puts its
  `data/*.csv` rows into the ID index for `lookup` and `ids`, never into SQLite
  (`arena_kit/data.py`, `_ids`). `personas.profile()`, `Negotiator.full_cost()` and the claims
  built from SQL (`po_lines`, `cost_drivers`, `documents`, `suppliers`) never see release rows,
  and document files resolve against the package root, not the release. Release IDs can still be
  cited. `design.md` says the release is "read at runtime"; that holds for `facts.json` only.
  → Read release rows through `pkg.ids(prefix)` / `pkg.lookup` (each row carries `root`) in
  `profile()` and the document claims. Check the CSV schema at 08:00.
- 2026-10-10 `data` **Most suppliers have no text.** Of 447 suppliers, 46 have documents, 31 news,
  18 quote remarks; the other 401 get the neutral profile (rate 7 %, no signals). A new supplier
  in the final is one of them or unknown to the package. → Its own e-mails and the release are
  the only persona source.
- 2026-10-10 `data` 15 of 108 quotes are priced per 100 (13) or per 1000 (2) pieces
  (`quotes.price_unit`). Rival-quote and order-history claims compare `unit_price` with the
  supplier's per-piece price without converting. → Divide by `price_unit` before comparing.
- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Structures only in unplayed cases** (case files): `tooling_eur` negotiable
  and lead time at most 84 days (P06), chargeback in the alternative (P12), index series PPI-C241
  in a clause (P16), fixed payment in a quality case (P12), a 3-part bundle (P15). Every case type
  and category goal appears in at least one hosted case. Only `incoterm` (D02) lies outside the
  fields the planner knows.

### Persona signals

- 2026-10-10 `data` **The patterns are not fitted to the practice suppliers**: the package's text
  is generated and its phrases recur, so all 10 suppliers of the unplayed cases get at least one
  trait. They miss other forms of the same phrases: "restructuring programme with its banks"
  (sup:70150), "negotiating with its banks" (sup:70280), "lowered its rating" (sup:70310),
  "bought their nickel and alloys forward" (sup:70730), "advertising free machine capacity"
  (sup:70250), "allocated in line with last year's call-offs" (sup:70410). "I cannot sign
  anything that lowers our margin now" (5 call notes) is a trait with no pattern. → Widen to word
  stems before the release adds new wording.
- 2026-10-10 `arena` **Supplier e-mails carry traits too:** 13 of 220 supplier e-mails in
  `exports/messages.jsonl` match `SIGNALS` (price_frozen sup:70530; spare_capacity sup:70210,
  70250, DEMO-J1; capacity_full sup:70240; cash_need sup:70210), including a sandbox supplier the
  package does not know. → Scanning each reply gives unknown suppliers a profile (untested in
  play).

### Tuning

- 2026-10-10 `arena` **Out-of-sample performance is unmeasured.** The 0.727 mean is in-sample:
  every constant was tuned on the same ten hosted cases and the other nine cannot be played.
  Runs of one case spread widely across v1 to v6 (P18 0.25 to 0.49 over seven runs, P08 0.40 to
  0.55), and with a model-written paragraph the wording changes per run while wording moves the
  price (`learnings.md`, takeaway 3). → Treat single-run moves below about 0.1 as noise.
- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Evidence behind each constant** in `buyer/policy.py` (from `git log -p`):

  | Constant | Cases behind it | Risk |
  |---|---|---|
  | `ANCHOR` leverage 0.78 | P05, P08 / P18 (one template) | medium |
  | `ANCHOR` routine 0.82 | P07 (P04 overridden by price_frozen) | medium to high |
  | `ANCHOR` quality_first 0.88 | P11 | medium |
  | `ANCHOR` stabilise 0.92, secure_supply 0.88 | none: always overridden in practice | high, untested |
  | `FRACTION` 0.3 | D01, D02, all hosted cases | low |
  | `DEEP` 0.06 | P05 (two job shops), D02 | medium |
  | price_frozen 0.95 | P03, P04 | low to medium |
  | capacity_full 0.93, budget 0.16, overtime 0.005 | P10, P05 sup:70240 | medium |
  | `near_cost` 0.97, budget 0.14 | P02 | high |

  → A hidden `stabilise` or `secure_supply` case with no override opens at an anchor never played.

## Sunday 08:00 checklist

1. `uv run arena data`; confirm `DataPackage("data/package").release` is not `None`.
2. List the release's `data/*.csv` and their columns; count supplier IDs new vs in the package.
3. Run every case file through `arena-sim` again with the release loaded.

1	"""The negotiation policy, per supplier thread: plan the non-price terms by C at the supplier's
2	own valuation, open below its quote, then move toward its counter round by round so it keeps
3	conceding, with verified claims spread over the rounds. Close on its final offer, its agreement or
4	the round limit; in relationship goals stop at the price where C is lowest.
5	
6	What the suppliers showed (sandbox and practice, `docs/learnings.md`):
7	- they concede only after a move from us and agree as soon as our sheet reaches the counter they
8	  would make, so our sheet stays below their counter until the end;
9	- every verified claim they take into account lowers where they stop, most of it in round 1;
10	- patience runs out at a cumulative gap of about 40 % between our sheets and their counters
11	  (summed per round, relative to their price), much earlier for a supplier selling near its cost
12	  or one that is fully booked: a final offer, or a walk-away;
13	- a large first concession means a deep floor: then we hold low instead of meeting it."""

228	        """Its reply changed some of our non-price terms (in its counter or an alternative): it told
229	        us what it values. Take a sheet's terms over when C at its price beats C of our plan at
230	        our counterpart of that price; when it insists on an index clause, take the clause that
231	        costs us least."""
232	        if not s.ours:
233	            return
234	        case = self.case
235	        standing_terms = sheets[0]["terms"]
236	        clause = standing_terms.get("index_clause")

242	            new = {**s.terms, "index_clause": clause}
243	            c_now = eco.cost(case, standing_terms, s.std, s.est)
244	            c_before = eco.cost(case, s.last_sheet, s.std, s.est)
245	            if eco.must_haves_ok(case, new, s.std) and c_now < c_before - 1.0:

247	            else:
248	                self.note(s.sid, "keep_terms", why="its index clause costs us more", c_now=c_now, c_before=c_before)
249	        best_c = eco.cost(case, eco.at_price(case, s.terms, self.their_price(s, standing_terms)), s.std, s.est)
250	        for sheet in sheets:
251	            terms = sheet["terms"]
252	            changed = {k: v for k, v in terms.items() if k != "unit_price" and k in s.terms and s.terms[k] != v}

254	            if not changed:
255	                continue
256	            new = {**s.terms, **changed}
257	            if not eco.must_haves_ok(case, new, s.std):
258	                continue
259	            if any((k, repr(v)) in s.tried for k, v in changed.items()):
260	                continue  # we were there before: no flip-flop
261	            c = eco.cost(case, eco.at_price(case, new, terms["unit_price"]), s.std, s.est)
262	            if c < best_c - max(1.0, 0.001 * best_c):
263	                best_c = c
264	                s.tried |= {(k, repr(s.terms.get(k))) for k in changed}

268	    def move(self, sid, threads, writer_s=llm.TIMEOUT_S):
269	        """The next message to this supplier: {"message": ...}, or None when the thread is done.

271	        case, s, events = self.case, self.sides[sid], threads[sid]
272	        self.writer_s = writer_s
273	        s.prev_state = s.state
274	        last = latest(events)
275	        status = last.get("status")
276	        if s.state == "ended" or status in ENDED:
277	            s.state = "ended"
278	            return None
279	        sheets = [sh for sh in last.get("term_sheets") or [] if sh.get("terms", {}).get("unit_price") is not None]
280	        if not sheets:
281	            s.state = "ended" if not standing(events)[0] else "done"
282	            return None
283	        s.std = standard_terms(events) or s.std
284	        fresh = s.last_reply is not last
285	        if fresh:
286	            terms_before = dict(s.terms)
287	            self.adopt(s, sheets)
288	            s.term_change = any(sheets[0]["terms"].get(k, v) != v for k, v in terms_before.items() if k != "unit_price")

290	            s.last_sheet = sheets[0]["terms"]
291	            s.last_reply = last
292	            s.asks = reader.asks(last.get("body"))
293	            self.read_signals(s, last.get("body"))
294	        theirs = s.theirs[-1]
295	        if s.state in ("mirror", "closing"):  # we sent its own sheet or our target: done
296	            s.state = "done"
297	            return None
298	        left = self.moves_left(s, events)
299	        if status in DONE or left <= 0:
300	            return self.finish(s, sheets, events, theirs, left)
301	        if s.target and theirs <= s.target * 1.002:
302	            # relationship goal: below the target a lower price costs more than it saves
303	            s.state = "closing"
304	            return self.send(s, [eco.at_price(case, s.terms, max(s.target, theirs))], [], events, theirs)
305	        if s.ours and theirs <= s.ours[-1]:  # it came below what we offered: take it
306	            return self.finish(s, sheets, events, theirs, left)
307	        price, n_claims = self.next_price(s, theirs)
308	        claims = self.pick(s, n_claims, threads)
309	        return self.send(s, [eco.at_price(case, s.terms, price)], claims, events, theirs)

311	    def moves_left(self, s, events):
312	        """Messages we may still send: the arena counts a late message as a round too."""
313	        return moves_left(self.case, events) - s.late

315	    def next_price(self, s, theirs):
316	        """Our next price at s.terms: open at the anchor; then a share of the gap, held low after a
317	        large concession, and within the patience budget."""
318	        if not s.ours:
319	            return s.anchor, FIRST_CLAIMS
320	        last = s.ours[-1]
321	        gap = (theirs - last) / theirs
322	        conceded = (s.theirs[-2] - theirs) / s.theirs[-2] if len(s.theirs) > 1 else 0.0
323	        share = FRACTION
324	        if len(s.ours) == 1 and conceded >= DEEP and not s.term_change:
325	            # a deep floor: a pure price drop this large means it moves fast on its own (job shops,
326	            # P05, D02); a drop that came with terms it added (an index clause, P08, P18) is not one
327	            share = 0.08
328	        left = max(0.0, s.budget - sum(s.gaps))
329	        new_gap = min(gap * (1 - share), left / 2)
330	        if s.budget < 0.2:  # a touchy supplier: small, steady gaps
331	            new_gap = min(new_gap, 0.015)
332	        price = theirs * (1 - new_gap)
333	        price = max(price, last * (1 + MIN_MOVE))
334	        price = min(price, theirs * 0.998)
335	        return round(max(price, last), 2), LATER_CLAIMS

337	    def finish(self, s, sheets, events, theirs, left):
338	        """Its final word, its agreement or our last message: if one of its alternatives costs us
339	        less than its standing sheet, send that sheet back so it agrees to it; else done."""
340	        case = self.case
341	        std = s.std
342	        c_stand = eco.cost(case, sheets[0]["terms"], std, s.est)
343	        alts = [(eco.cost(case, sh["terms"], std, s.est), sh) for sh in sheets[1:]]
344	        alts = [(c, sh) for c, sh in alts if eco.must_haves_ok(case, sh["terms"], std)]
345	        if alts and left > 0:
346	            c, sh = min(alts, key=lambda r: r[0])
347	            if c < c_stand - 1.0:
348	                s.state = "mirror"
349	                terms = {k: v for k, v in sh["terms"].items() if k in case["negotiable"]}
350	                return self.send(s, [eco.complete_offer(case, terms)], [], events, theirs)
351	        s.state = "done"
352	        return None

331	    """The Live Final: wait for each wave, play its cases in parallel within the wave's cap. No
332	    human may restart it, so nothing here raises: a failed poll is polled again, a crashed case is
333	    resumed once (the arena names the running session on a second open)."""
334	    started, closed, caps = {}, set(), {}

336	    def one(case, deadline):
337	        for attempt in range(2):
338	            try:
339	                return play_case(RemoteTable(client, case), case["case_id"], pkg, deadline, complete)
340	            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - one broken case must not stop the others
341	                log.exception("%s failed (attempt %d)", case["case_id"], attempt + 1)
342	                err = e
343	                time.sleep(2)

346	    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=parallel) as pool:
347	        while len(closed) < waves or not all(f.done() for f in started.values()):
348	            try:
349	                cases = client.cases("final")
350	            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - 403 before the first wave, a network blip: poll again
351	                if not (isinstance(e, ArenaError) and e.status == 403):
352	                    log.warning("case list: %s", e)
353	                cases = []
354	            for case in cases:
355	                if not case.get("open"):
356	                    closed.add(case["wave"])
357	                    continue
358	                if case.get("seconds_left") is not None:
359	                    caps[case["wave"]] = time.time() + case["seconds_left"]
360	                if case["case_id"] not in started and case.get("seconds_left"):
361	                    log.warning("wave %s: %s", case["wave"], case["case_id"])
362	                    started[case["case_id"]] = pool.submit(one, case, functools.partial(caps.get, case["wave"]))

def closing_terms(case, terms, standard=None):
    """The terms a deal would close on: the term sheet, then the supplier's standard terms (from
    its quote PDF) for anything left out, then the case's fixed terms; gaps from the buyer's plan.
    """
    b = case["buyer"]
    freight = b["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    plan = {
        "volume_per_year": b["need_per_year"],
        "contract_months": round(12 * b["horizon_years"]),
        "payment_days": b["reference_payment_days"],
        "lead_time_days": b["need_lead_time_days"],
        # an unknown Incoterm counts as the costliest: a cautious buyer does not assume DAP
        "incoterm": max(freight, key=freight.get),
    }
    t = dict(plan)
    for layer in (standard or {}, case.get("fixed_terms", {}), terms):
        t.update({k: v for k, v in layer.items() if v is not None or k not in plan})
    return t


def horizon_start(case):
    """The horizon starts at the fixed or the earliest possible effective date."""
    fixed = case.get("fixed_terms", {}).get("effective_date")
    options = [o for o in case.get("term_options", {}).get("effective_date", []) if o]
    first = fixed or (min(options) if options else None)
    return date.fromisoformat(first) if first else None


def _years(case, t):
    """Years of the horizon a deal covers; a single order (0 months) counts as one year's lot.
    A commitment beyond the horizon neither costs nor earns."""
    months = t["contract_months"]
    return min(months / 12 if months else 1.0, case["buyer"]["horizon_years"])


def _units_before(case, t, years):
    """Units bought between the horizon start and the date a new price takes effect."""
    start = horizon_start(case)
    if not t.get("effective_date") or start is None:
        return 0.0
    lag = (date.fromisoformat(t["effective_date"]) - start).days / 365
    return t["volume_per_year"] * min(max(lag, 0.0), years)


def supplier_value(case, terms, supplier):
    """What a deal is worth to the supplier per unit, in cash: the price at its standard terms that
    would pay it the same. `supplier` is your estimate of it:
      standard       its standard terms (quote PDF, `docs.standard_terms`)
      interest_rate  what money now is worth to it per year (more to a supplier short of cash)
      usual_rate     its usual cost of money (default: interest_rate); tooling paid up front is
                     worth more to it when cash is dearer than usual
      ppm            the defect rate it really achieves (default: its standard ppm commitment)
      extra          EUR per unit it gains (+) or spends (-) beyond these items, e.g. overtime for
                     a faster delivery or idle capacity a larger volume fills (default 0)
    Contract length and an index clause are security, not cash: they do not count here."""
    b, std = case["buyer"], {**supplier["standard"], **case.get("fixed_terms", {})}
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, std)
    years = _years(case, t)
    sold = t["volume_per_year"] * years
    old = _units_before(case, t, years) / sold  # sold at the current price
    rate = supplier["interest_rate"]
    pay = 1 - rate * (t["payment_days"] - std["payment_days"]) / 360
    cash_now = 1 + (rate - supplier.get("usual_rate", rate)) * years / 2
    freight = b["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    ppm = supplier.get("ppm", std.get("ppm_commitment") or 0)
    return (
        t["unit_price"] * (1 - old) * pay
        + old * (b.get("current_unit_price") or 0.0) * pay
        + freight[t["incoterm"]]
        - freight[std["incoterm"]]  # it carries the freight leg
        + ((t.get("tooling_eur") or 0) - (std.get("tooling_eur") or 0)) / sold * cash_now
        - ppm / 1e6 * ((t.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0) - (std.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0))
        + supplier.get("extra", 0.0)
    )


def _soft(gap):
    """Margin points below the sustainable margin, as they cost: none above it, quadratic over
    the first 5 points, linear beyond - no kink."""
    if gap <= 0:
        return 0.0
    return gap * gap / 10 if gap <= 5 else gap - 2.5


def relationship_cost(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None, value=None):
    """Strategic and bottleneck goals only: EUR for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier
    below `sustainable_margin_pct`, per year covered. `supplier["full_cost"]` (EUR per unit) is your
    estimate of its full cost; `value` overrides `supplier_value`. Without an estimate: 0."""
    b = case["buyer"]
    per_point, sustainable = b.get("relationship_eur_per_point"), b.get("sustainable_margin_pct")
    if b.get("category_goal") not in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS or not per_point or not sustainable or not supplier:
        return 0.0
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    worth = value if value is not None else supplier_value(case, t, supplier)
    margin = (worth - supplier["full_cost"]) / worth * 100
    return per_point * _soft(sustainable - margin) * _years(case, t)


def cost_breakdown(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None):
    """C by part. `standard`: the supplier's standard terms for anything the term sheet leaves out.
    `supplier`: your estimate of the supplier for the relationship term (`supplier_value`)."""
    b, t = case["buyer"], closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    if t.get("unit_price") is None:
        raise ValueError("no unit_price: a term sheet without a price has no cost")
    years = _years(case, t)
    committed = t["volume_per_year"] * years  # bought, needed or not
    covered = min(t["volume_per_year"], b["need_per_year"]) * years
    pre = _units_before(case, t, years)
    at_new_price = (committed - pre) * t["unit_price"]
    spend = pre * (b.get("current_unit_price") or t["unit_price"]) + at_new_price
    per_defect = b.get("cost_per_defect", 0)
    defect_cost = per_defect - min(t.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0, per_defect)
    index = index_risk = 0.0
    if clause := t.get("index_clause"):
        path = b.get("index_paths", {}).get(clause["series"], 0.0)
        moved = max(0.0, abs(path) - clause["deadband_pct"] / 100)
        index = at_new_price * clause["material_share"] * moved * math.copysign(1, path)
        index_risk = at_new_price * clause["material_share"] * b.get("index_risk_pct", 0) / 100
    uncovered = (b["need_per_year"] * b["horizon_years"] - covered) * b["fallback_unit_price"]
    need = b["need_lead_time_days"]
    return {
        "price": spend,
        "uncovered_need": uncovered,
        "fallback_risk": uncovered * b.get("fallback_risk_pct", 0) / 100,
        "payment_terms": spend * b["interest_rate"] * (b["reference_payment_days"] - t["payment_days"]) / 360,
        "freight": committed * b["freight_eur_per_unit"][t["incoterm"]],
        "late_delivery": b.get("late_cost_per_day", 0) * max(0, t["lead_time_days"] - need),
        "quality": committed * (t.get("ppm_commitment") or 0) / 1e6 * defect_cost,
        "tooling": t.get("tooling_eur") or 0.0,
        "index_clause": index,
        "index_risk": index_risk,
        "relationship": relationship_cost(case, t, supplier=supplier),
    }


def total_cost(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None):
    """C in EUR; infinite for terms without a price (e.g. a supplier that quotes none), so such a
    sheet is never the cheapest and never beats an alternative."""
    if closing_terms(case, terms, standard).get("unit_price") is None:
        return math.inf
    return round(sum(cost_breakdown(case, terms, standard, supplier).values()), 2)


def score(c_open, c_deal, c_best):
    if c_deal is None:
        return 0.0
    if c_open - c_best <= 0.01:  # no room to negotiate: matching the best is full marks
        return 1.0 if c_deal <= c_best + 0.01 else 0.0
    return min(1.0, max(0.0, (c_open - c_deal) / (c_open - c_best)))


def must_haves_ok(case, terms, standard=None):
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    for m in case["buyer"].get("must_haves", []):
        value = t.get(m["field"])
        if value is None and m["op"] not in ("==", "!="):
            return False
        if not OPS[m["op"]](value, m["value"]):
            return False
    return True


def snap(case, field, value):
    """The allowed value closest to `value` (case `term_options`), else `value` unchanged."""
    options = case.get("term_options", {}).get(field)
    if not options or value in options:
        return value
    if isinstance(value, int | float) and all(isinstance(o, int | float) for o in options):
        return min(options, key=lambda o: (abs(o - value), o))
    return options[0]

}

def read_document(name, data):
    """The text of an attachment: PDF pages, XLSX rows (formulas as written), or plain text."""
    if name.endswith(".pdf"):
        from pypdf import PdfReader

        return "\n".join(p.extract_text() for p in PdfReader(io.BytesIO(data)).pages)
    if name.endswith(".xlsx"):

content.text:
Probes are done and I have everything I need. Writing up the assessment, the experiment results and the three architecture proposals now.

## What works, what does not, and where the 0.08 goes

**What works.** The cost engine is sound: no accepted sheet has broken a must-have or lost to the alternative since v1, and every binding number comes from `arena_kit.total_cost`. The term planner wins where the kit's supplier model is right (P10 lead time, free 24 months, P05 overtime). The RFQ scheduler holds the all-team record on P05. The robustness layer (guards, wave loop, resume, writer budget) is the right shape for an unattended final. The concession walk is near-optimal against job shops and the sandbox foundry (D01 0.99).

**Where the gap is.** Against the best per case across all teams our mean is 0.73 and the composite is 0.82. Four cases carry 0.81 of the 0.89 total gap. In all four the supplier gives 3 to 5 counters and stops, and our round count is the binding constraint, not our anchor.

| Case | Goal | Ours | Record | Gap | Our deal vs. record, EUR | What limits us |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P02 | stabilise | 0.51 | 0.85 | 0.34 | 16,100 | Nordmark gives 4 tiny counters; fixed price only |
| P18 | leverage | 0.49 | 0.68 | 0.19 | 13,900 | index clause costs 7,900 of it; 3 counters |
| P08 | leverage | 0.57 | 0.73 | 0.16 | 28,300 | index clause costs 31,800; 4 counters |
| P11 | quality_first | 0.71 | 0.81 | 0.10 | 9,200 | floor 45.50 at any ppm; wants payment, which is fixed |
| other six | | | | 0.09 total | | within noise of the records |

**What does not work.**
- The planner prices every lever at the kit's `supplier_value`, which says contract length and index clauses are "security, not cash". The bots disagree: Nordmark paid about 6% of price for a copper clause with a 5% deadband that costs us 0.8%. The planner can never find that trade because its supplier model forbids it.
- Claims move nothing on groups and distributors ("does not change our calculation" in 13 of 13 P08 runs). The claim bank is tuned for the one supplier type it moves (family foundries).
- We end threads ourselves: the walk goes to 0.2% under the counter, the bot says "agreed", and 5 rounds go unused. Slow-walking P08 tonight (12% of the gap per round) got a fifth counter and our best P08 (0.59), but the distributors still stop after 4 to 5 counters whatever the path.
- The words lever is almost unused. The e-mail is a template plus one model paragraph forbidden from carrying any number. D01 showed 1.2% from one sentence, and the round-1 counter varies about 1.3% between runs with identical sheets. On P08, P18 and P11 no sheet lever explains the record, which leaves wording and trade framing as the open hypothesis.

**What is overfitted.** The anchor table per goal (stabilise and secure_supply anchors were never played unoverridden), the near-cost and capacity-full budgets (one case each), the deep-floor rule (P05, D02), and the "take the distributor's clause" rule, which is correct for Donautal and Werdenfels and wrong for Nordmark. The persona and ask regexes are fitted to the generated phrasing in the package. The working tree also keeps changing under me from another session (FRACTION 0.4 earlier, now claims.py); I did not edit any repo file.

## What ten practice sessions showed tonight

I ran scripted round-1 variants with a slow walk afterwards. The bots are deterministic, so one session per variant is a clean measurement. Harness and logs are in the scratchpad; the sessions are pullable with `uv run buyer pull`.

| Variant | Session | Result |
|---|---|---|
| P02 copper clause, 5% deadband, 358 at 90 days | 491006cd111217a3 | agreed at once, 0.67 (our best was 0.51), "we can even improve upon your proposed base price" |
| P02 same, two sheets (clause vs fixed) | 91d2b5ad7501ce55 | it picked the clause sheet, 0.67 |
| P02 same clause, anchor 345 | ea485d8c4db527aa | counters 351.05, 349.85, 349.35, 349.05, then it withdrew (below its cost) |
| P08 clause in round 1, two clauses, fixed 24 months | d025739…, cd533e8…, 7b029b9… | 5.38 to 5.39, no better than asking fixed; fixed 24 months refused again |
| P08 slow walk | 50502ff781d898c6 | 5.31, 0.59, our best P08 |
| P08 forecast-volume words | 4ad7436e68138dae | 5.36, no effect |
| P11 three-sheet menu; 800 ppm alone | 1f36a83…, a74b891… | floor 45.50 at 300 and at 800 ppm; 300 ppm is right |

Calibrating Nordmark's full cost from the arena's own relationship charge (about 368.6) shows the clause price must stop near 361 at 90 days, where C is lowest: score about 0.73, not the 0.67 of the agreed anchor and not the 349 the bot would go to. The engine's relationship optimum already does this once the terms carry the clause. The same structure exists in the unplayed P14 and P16 cases, so it will likely appear in the final.

## Three architectures

**1. Elicit the supplier's valuation instead of assuming the kit's.** Keep the engine. Round 1 sends up to three sheets of equal C to us that differ in one lever each (clause and deadband, payment, ppm, months). Its standing sheet and alternatives give its price per lever. From round 2 the planner uses that observed valuation, picks the structure with the lowest C, and recomputes the relationship optimum on it. Menus only where a lever is worth more than 0.5% of spend, since distributors give only 4 counters. Proven today on P02 (+0.16 in one session, about +0.22 at the optimum). Half a day, low risk. This is my recommendation for tonight.

**2. Opponent model with lookahead.** Fit the bots' observed rules from the 135 sessions: round-1 counter as a cap, a shrinking concession schedule, a fixed counter count per archetype, withdrawal below cost in relationship goals. Identify the archetype online from reply delay, validity and the first concession, then choose each move by simulating the remaining rounds. This replaces the constant table with something that adapts to a stranger within two rounds. One day, medium risk; a Sunday-morning item only if 1 is merged and stable.

**3. Model-in-the-loop negotiator with code guards.** A strong model reads the supplier's e-mail and persona notes, picks among code-priced candidate sheets, and writes the whole e-mail, with the guard enforcing that every figure and ID comes from code and nothing leaks. This is the only candidate aimed at the unexplained residual on P08, P18 and P11, where no sheet lever accounts for the record and the bots are LLM personas reacting to wording. The 200 euros covers thousands of calls; the latency budget exists. Highest variance; test as an A/B of three runs each on P08, P18 and P11 (9 sessions) before deciding.

Order: 1 now, 3 as an A/B tonight if time allows, 2 only as polish. The learnings entries for the clause finding and the P08 counter count are ready to paste; I left `docs/learnings.md` untouched because another session has uncommitted edits in it.
Feel free to test all of that :)

Setting up an isolated worktree so the shared checkout stays untouched, then implementing architecture 1 (round-1 lever menu with the observed valuation driving the planner), then the architecture 3 A/B (model-written e-mails under the code guard).
